entities.name: GlmU
observations: The 462-residue query is a strong GlmU homolog: 53.6% identity and 97.4% query coverage to reviewed Thermotoga GlmU proteins, E-values ~10^-146 to 10^-147.
GlmU is a bifunctional enzyme with an N-terminal UDP-GlcNAc pyrophosphorylase module, a linker, and a C-terminal glucosamine-1-phosphate N-acetyltransferase module.
The enzyme is reported as cytosolic and homotrimeric; sequence-based assignment has moderate homology support.
A Pfam scan supports an N-terminal NTP-transferase region and C-terminal Hexapep/Hexapep_2 acetyltransferase-associated regions.

entities.name: GlcN1P acetylation
observations: Alpha-D-glucosamine 1-phosphate + acetyl-CoA yields N-acetyl-alpha-D-glucosamine 1-phosphate + CoA + H(+). This is EC 2.3.1.157 and Rhea RHEA:13725.
The reaction is catalyzed by the C-terminal acetyltransferase domain of GlmU.

entities.name: UDP-GlcNAc formation
observations: N-acetyl-alpha-D-glucosamine 1-phosphate + UTP + H(+) yields UDP-N-acetyl-alpha-D-glucosamine + diphosphate. This is EC 2.7.7.23 and Rhea RHEA:13509.
The reaction is catalyzed by the N-terminal pyrophosphorylase domain of GlmU and requires Mg(2+) according to reviewed homolog annotation.

entities.name: UDP-GlcNAc biosynthesis
observations: GlmU catalyzes the final two sequential steps of bacterial UDP-N-acetylglucosamine biosynthesis, connecting glucosamine-1-phosphate and UTP to UDP-GlcNAc.
UDP-GlcNAc supports peptidoglycan biosynthesis and, in suitable bacteria, lipid A/outer-membrane biogenesis.

entities.name: GlmU sequence properties
observations: The query is 462 amino acids, approximately 50.8 kDa, with predicted pI 8.05 and mildly basic net charge near pH 7.
These are sequence-derived estimates and do not account for oligomerization, ligands, processing, or modifications.
